Find hits with ROAST or FRY

Source: R/find_roast_hit.R
find_roast_hit.Rd

Finds the genes whose barcodes are depleted (or enriched) in the comparison given by the contrast, using the ROAST method (mroast) or its fast approximation FRY (fry). ROAST is a self-contained gene set test: it tests whether the barcodes of a gene change, without comparing them with the other barcodes, so it is not affected by the number of genes with an effect. It needs replicates in both groups (see Details).

Usage

find_roast_hit(
  screenR_Object,
  matrix_model,
  contrast,
  nrot = 9999,
  number_barcode = 3,
  direction = c("Down", "Up"),
  p_val = NULL,
  fdr = 0.05,
  seed = NULL,
  method = c("roast", "fry"),
  fdr_method = c("BH", "storey")
)

Arguments

screenR_Object

The ScreenR object obtained using create_screenr_object.

matrix_model

The design matrix of the linear model, for example created with create_design_matrix (or with model.matrix).

contrast

The comparison to test: the name or index of a column of matrix_model, a numeric contrast vector (for example created with create_contrast) or a one-column matrix created with makeContrasts.

nrot

The number of random rotations used by method = "roast" (default 9999). More rotations give more precise p-values and allow smaller ones (the smallest is 1 / (nrot + 1)), but take longer. Not used by method = "fry".

number_barcode

Only genes with more than number_barcode barcodes are tested (default 3, so a gene needs at least 4 barcodes). The barcodes of a gene are tested together as a set, so this is not a number of barcodes that must change.

direction

The direction of the change: "Down" (default) for depleted genes or "Up" for enriched genes.

p_val

An optional cut off on the raw (not adjusted) one-sided p-value: only genes with PValue < p_val are returned. By default (NULL) only the FDR cut off is used.

fdr

The FDR threshold: only genes with an FDR lower than or equal to this value are returned (default 0.05). Use fdr = 1 to return all the genes with the given direction.

seed

An optional random seed. ROAST uses random rotations, so the p-values change slightly between runs; setting a seed makes the result reproducible. The random number state of the session is restored afterwards. Not used by method = "fry".

method

"roast" (default, random rotations) or "fry" (fast exact approximation, recommended for large screens).

fdr_method

How the FDR is computed: "BH" (Benjamini-Hochberg, the default) or "storey" (Benjamini-Hochberg multiplied by the estimated proportion of genes without effect, less conservative when many genes have an effect).

Value

A tibble with one row for each hit in the requested direction and the columns returned by mroast (Gene, NGenes, PropDown, PropUp, Direction, PValue, FDR, PValue.Mixed, FDR.Mixed) or by fry (without PropDown and PropUp), plus Log2FC, the median log2 fold change of the barcodes of the gene. NGenes is the number of barcodes of the gene. PValue is the one-sided p-value for the requested direction and FDR is computed from it over all the genes; PValue.Mixed and FDR.Mixed are those of limma (a change in either direction).

Details

The raw counts are modelled with edgeR (the dispersion is estimated with estimateDisp) and the barcodes of each gene are tested together. The p-values are computed with random rotations (method = "roast", whose smallest possible p-value is 1 / (nrot + 1)) or with fry (method = "fry"), a fast and exact approximation of roast with an unlimited number of rotations, which is faster and gives continuous p-values. The two-sided p-values are converted into one-sided p-values for the requested direction and the FDR is computed from them over all the tested genes.

Since roast tests each gene on its own barcodes, its power depends on the variability between replicates: it needs replicates in both the treated and the control group and has little power with two replicates or noisy data. With a single control sample (for example a plasmid library) it finds almost no hits; in this case use find_camera_hit or find_gene_zscore_hit, which compare each gene with the other genes. Being self-contained, roast also reports genes whose barcodes change because of off-target effects.

See also

find_camera_hit, find_gene_zscore_hit, find_time_hit, summarise_hits, plot_barcode_hit, create_design_matrix, create_contrast

Examples

object <- get0("object", envir = asNamespace("ScreenR"))
matrix_model <- create_design_matrix(object)
contrast <- create_contrast(matrix_model, treatment = "Treated",
    control = "Control")

result <- find_roast_hit(object,
    matrix_model = matrix_model,
    contrast = contrast, nrot = 100, seed = 42
)
#> Warning: 3rows with all zero counts
head(result)
#> # A tibble: 0 × 10
#> # ℹ 10 variables: Gene <chr>, NGenes <int>, PropDown <dbl>, PropUp <dbl>,
#> #   Direction <fct>, PValue <dbl>, FDR <dbl>, PValue.Mixed <dbl>,
#> #   FDR.Mixed <dbl>, Log2FC <dbl>

# FRY: faster, with continuous p-values (fdr = 1 returns all the genes)
result <- find_roast_hit(object,
    matrix_model = matrix_model,
    contrast = contrast, method = "fry", fdr = 1
)
#> Warning: 3rows with all zero counts
head(result)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>   Gene     NGenes Direction   PValue   FDR PValue.Mixed FDR.Mixed  Log2FC
#>   <chr>     <int> <fct>        <dbl> <dbl>        <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 Gene_173     10 Down      0.000236 0.126      0.00330     0.588 -0.429 
#> 2 Gene_15      10 Down      0.00158  0.396      0.0226      0.998 -0.272 
#> 3 Gene_457     10 Down      0.00228  0.396      0.0446      0.998 -0.0230
#> 4 Gene_446     10 Down      0.00341  0.396      0.562       0.998 -0.131 
#> 5 Gene_121     10 Down      0.00379  0.396      0.00103     0.549 -0.194 
#> 6 Gene_293     10 Down      0.00508  0.396      0.00261     0.588 -0.108
